scripts.db:migrate:
node -e "console.error('
  pnpm db:migrate is disabled.

  prisma migrate dev is a DEVELOPMENT command. When it detects drift between
  the migration history and the database it offers to RESET -- dropping and
  recreating the schema. Production has 80+ tables and no migration history at
  all, so it would detect drift on the very first run.

  For a LOCAL or THROWAWAY database:
      pnpm db:migrate:local

  For PRODUCTION: prisma migrate deploy, which never resets.
      pnpm db:migrate:deploy
'); process.exit(1)"
scripts.db:migrate:reset:
node -e "console.error('
  pnpm db:migrate:reset is disabled.

  prisma migrate reset DROPS AND RECREATES THE ENTIRE SCHEMA. There is no
  partial version of this and no undo. Against production it destroys every
  call record, lead and recording reference in the database.

  For a LOCAL or THROWAWAY database:
      pnpm db:migrate:reset:local

  If you are trying to fix a broken local database, that is the command you
  want. If you are pointed at anything else, stop.
'); process.exit(1)"
scripts.db:push:
node -e "console.error('
  pnpm db:push is disabled.

  prisma db push performs a DESTRUCTIVE schema sync: it computes a diff and
  applies it with no reviewable artifact and no record of what changed. This
  is how the production database came to have 80 tables and no migration
  history, and running it from apps/api has targeted production before now.

  For a LOCAL or THROWAWAY database (CI containers, a scratch db):
      pnpm db:push:local

  For PRODUCTION: write a migration and apply it with
      pnpm db:migrate:deploy
  See .agent/workflows/deploy.md
'); process.exit(1)"
